recentItems.title: Protests turn violent in The Gambia over rolling blackouts
recentItems.description:
Protests in The Gambia have turned violent after months of power outages that have disrupted essential public services like water supplies during the hot season. Demonstrators are calling on Gambian President Adama Barrow to resign.

recentItems.title: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia may signal shortage of long-range weapons, analyst says
recentItems.description:
Houthi attacks on southern Saudi Arabia have continued for a second consecutive day, as Saudi-backed air strikes hit four areas in Yemen, including Taiz and Hodeidah.
In an interview with Al Jazeera, security and defence analyst Wolfgang Pusztai said the Houthis’ focus on targets near the Yemeni border suggests they may be running out of longer-range missiles and drones, partly because of the blockade of Yemeni harbours.
He said the intent is to show Saudi Arabia that “if you are fighting war in Yemen, we will bring the war back home to you”, aiming to break Riyadh’s will to sustain its campaign.
However, Pusztai doubted this would work, saying Yemen is too important to Saudi Arabia, while the Houthis are seeking control of the Red Sea coast and the Bab al-Mandeb Strait.
Pakistan has warned Iran to rein in the Houthis, and Pusztai noted that Pakistan has already deployed a fighter squadron, an air defence squadron and ground troops to Saudi Arabia, calling this a strong signal to both the Houthis and Tehran.
He said the Mecca Defence Pact, previously a “paper tiger” in terms of mutual defence, could now gain greater significance, while Saudi Arabia is already being drawn into a wider war in Yemen with almost full-intensity fighting that is unlikely to end soon.

recentItems.title: Syria Kurdish forces integration: Future for female YPJ remains uncertain
recentItems.description:
For 15 years, Kurdish women of the YPJ fought on Syria’s front lines, notably against ISIL. Now they’re told by the government that Syrian society “isn’t ready” for women in the army, a claim they reject as 979 female fighters killed in combat underscore their sacrifices. 

YPJ leaders say they’re negotiating to integrate around 1,500 women, even as they train for battles they may not be allowed to fight. 

Bernard Smith reports from Qamishli in North Eastern Syria.

recentItems.title: Trump Offers “Dividend” Cash Pledge to Energise Republican Base
recentItems.description:
Donald Trump comes to Dallas to energise Republicans as they face poor polling and tight races across the country. On stage, he touts his record, jokes about renaming the Strait of Hormuz the “Trump Strait” and promises a $5,000 “Trump Dividend” if Republicans win full control of Congress. Inside the arena, loyalists say he is “saving America”, while outside many voters blame him for war talk, economic pain and rising gas prices. 

Al Jazeera's Richard Gaisford reports from Dallas.

recentItems.title: US announces $45m in security funding, additional naval vessels for Ecuador
recentItems.description:
In Quito, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio meets President Daniel Noboa as Washington deepens security ties with Ecuador against drug trafficking groups. 
Rubio pledges $45m in extra funding and more military equipment under the Shield of the Americas initiative, while U.S. forces extend operations into the Pacific, targeting suspected narco vessels. Fishermen describe boats sunk, detentions and killings, as judges free some detainees for lack of evidence and concerns grow over US intervention. 

Al Jazeera's Teresa Bo reports from Quito, Ecuador.
